events.text: Graft Row dock: a long gantry of welded plate, lit by a thousand work lamps, staffed by Gauntlings in every stage of repair. A sign over the airlock reads ASK ME ABOUT MY ARM. The dock foreman, Gasket, is already telling you about hers. It involves a reactor, a sunrise and a man called Dennis.

outcomes.text: Forty minutes later you know more about Dennis than you ever wanted, and the crew are in tears of laughter. Gasket tips you a spare coil for being a good audience.
The story has a second half. And a third. And a sequel about Dennis's cousin. You leave, richer in anecdote, poorer in time.
You tell the story of the worst day of your life, with embellishments. Gasket listens, nods, and says 'Not bad. Needs more explosion.' She adds one. Everyone cheers.
Gasket tops it in a single sentence. You lose with grace, and are bought a drink.

Your Gauntling and Gasket line up their arms side by side, name every bolt, and settle whose is older. It is a tie. They hug, with a sound like a scrapyard falling down a hill. The dock gives you a discount on the whole gantry.

choices.text: [Mire] Ask if anyone has been on fire.

outcomes.text: Gasket's lamp lights. 'Do tell,' she says. Your Mire and the dock foreman swap fire stories for an hour, comparing burns like medals. The dock gives your Mire a welding mask as a trophy.

events.text: The yard's Gauntlings are holding a contest: Best Accident. A circle of crates, forty contestants, a panel of three judges with scoring cards. The current leader lost both legs to a reactor, a goat and a pair of dice. A banner reads NO BORING ACCIDENTS. A judge looks at you. 'You. Do you have one?'

choices.text: Tell the story of your worst day.

outcomes.text: You tell it. The judges listen politely and give you 6, 6 and 7, the best score for a non-Gauntling in the history of the contest. They award you a medal made of washers, and a printed copy of the results.
You tell it. The judges give you 2, 2 and 3. 'Too safe,' says one. 'Try falling off something.' The crowd laughs with you, mostly.

choices.text: Say you have never had an accident.

outcomes.text: The circle goes quiet. A judge puts down her card. 'No accidents,' she says, as if you had confessed to a crime. 'Then what are you for?' You are escorted gently out, with a bag of consolation washers.

choices.text: [Gauntling] Tell the one about your own arm.

outcomes.text: Your Gauntling takes the floor, rolls up a sleeve, and tells the story of their arm. It ends with an explosion, an apology and a man on fire. The judges score it 9, 9, 10. They award the grand prize: a crate of spare parts, a cup, the title of Best Accident, and the results.

choices.text: [Basalt] Say it was not an accident, it was erosion.

outcomes.text: Your Basalt says, slowly, 'It happened over six hundred years.' Silence. Then the judges applaud. 'Longest accident ever,' says one. They give your Basalt a lifetime achievement award: a washer.

events.text: The sky ahead flickers violet: an ion storm, rolling over the yard in a wall of static. Every Gauntling on the Row is lashing down hatches, killing lamps and wrapping their dreadlocks in foil. 'Ion!' someone yells. 'Get your arm in!' A Gauntling sits down on the dock, folds her hands and waits to be stunned, with the air of a woman who has done this before.

outcomes.text: You tuck in behind the yard's old reactor shield as the storm roars over. Inside the shelter the Gauntlings play cards in the dark, laughing, waiting for their pins to clear. When it passes, the whole Row cheers, and deals you in.
The storm finds a gap in the shield. Every system on your ship flickers and every Gauntling in the room freezes for three seconds, mid-sentence. You wait politely.
A discharge arcs through the hull. The lights die, the helm freezes, and you drift for ten minutes while everything reboots.

choices.text: Fly into the storm to harvest ion-charged scrap.

outcomes.text: The storm fills your hold with scrap magnetised in the shape of a lightning bolt. You come out crackling, wired and rich.
The storm fries half your systems and stuns you for a few seconds. You get out with the haul and a ringing in every ear.
A discharge goes through the bunk room and finds you without foil. You live. You will not forget.
A discharge finds a crew member in the corridor. You find the haul, and not them.

choices.text: Fly into the storm to harvest ion-charged scrap.

outcomes.text: The storm fills your hold with scrap magnetised in the shape of a lightning bolt. You come out crackling, wired and rich.
The storm fries half your systems and stuns you for a few seconds. You get out with the haul and a ringing in every ear.
A discharge goes through the bunk room and finds you without foil. You live. You will not forget.
A discharge finds you in the corridor. You come to on the deck with the haul and a ringing in every tooth, and half the ship's lights out.

Your Gauntling, ion-prone, wraps themselves in foil and stands in the middle of the Row, shouting orders in a voice like a cannon. The Row lashes down in record time. When the storm hits it frizzes their hair and stuns them for three seconds. They do not mind. They are a hero, and a card player's log lands in their lap.
The storm catches your Gauntling mid-sentence, and they freeze for eleven seconds with a heroic face. It is photographed.
Ion hurts crystal. Your Prismatic hums anyway, a low steady counter-note that rolls the static aside in a ring round the ship. The Row watches, awed. Your Prismatic, shaking, is helped to a bunk.
The static finds your Prismatic's facets. They take it twice over. They hold the note anyway.

events.text: A breaker's yard: a hulk of a dead warship half-scrapped by a crew who ran out of money in the middle. Cut-through bulkheads, stacks of numbered plate, a sign on the gate reading BACK IN FIVE. The sign has been there a decade. A cutting torch sits in the middle of the hangar, still lit, in a puddle of old slag.

choices.text: Finish the job and take your share.

outcomes.text: You cut the next three decks, number each plate in chalk, and stack them neat. The yard's owner shows up two hours later, looks at the work, says 'Huh,' and pays you in scrap.
A bulkhead lets go and takes a cutting arm with it. You salvage the arm, and the rest.
In the keel, a hatch no one bothered with: a locker of unused plate. Whole.
The torch is a very good torch. It has a name scratched into the grip: DENNIS. You decide not to ask.

choices.text: [Tinkerer] Spot the dead man's switch before you cut.

outcomes.text: Your tinkerer examines the half-cut bulkhead for ten seconds, then points to a thin wire the previous crew missed. 'That is a charge,' they say. You leave it alone and cut around it. The yard's owner, later, cries.
Your Grundl hefts plate like loaves. By evening the yard is stacked, a month ahead of schedule. The owner pays in scrap and an invitation to sit.

events.text: Lefty's Swap: a long table covered in arms, legs, eyes, hands and lamps, in every size and finish. Everything is for sale or trade at a rate set by Lefty's mood, which is currently good. 'Looking for an upgrade?' he asks. 'Or a downgrade? We do both. We do sideways.'

outcomes.text: Lefty hands over a coil of cable, a tin of washers and a lamp that works. 'Guaranteed,' he says. 'Mostly.'
The part is excellent. It is also, you realise later, someone's thumb. It comes with a note: ABOUT DENNIS.
Lefty weighs your scrap on a scale shaped like a hand, tuts, and pays more than he has to. 'Proper scrap,' he says. 'None of this fancy stuff.'

Your Gauntling and Lefty compare spare arms for an hour, trade a hand for a better one, and part with a promise to write. Your Gauntling returns stronger in a way nobody can quite name. You get a bag of parts for the ship, and a very old note.
Your tinkerer fixes the counter, rewires the lamps and tunes the scale. Lefty can't believe it. 'It is like having a new body,' he says. He pays in parts.

choices.text: Look over the table and leave.

outcomes.text: You look at the table for a long time. A hand waves at you from a bucket. You wave back. Lefty says 'Pleasure,' and means it.

events.text: A bounty hunter named Marrow, in a ship called Reclaimed, is working the Row. The warrant: one Gauntling, wanted by the Gantry Clan for an unpaid arm. 'Stolen goods,' she says, tapping a screen. 'The arm is clan property. It stays with the clan.' The Gauntling in question stands behind her, arms folded, looking at her arm like a man looking at a bad sandwich.

outcomes.text: You help. The Gauntling is escorted to the clan. Marrow pays well. You do not feel great about it. The Row watches you leave in total, terrible silence.
The Gauntling puts up a spirited fight, and wins, and runs. Marrow is furious. She pays you half for the effort and is nowhere to be found.

You distract Marrow with a long and complicated question about her warrant. The Gauntling slips out of the airlock into the yard. Marrow looks at you for a very long time. 'Next time,' she says. A copy of the warrant is left in your hold.
Marrow figures it out and is cross. A scuffle follows. The Gauntling escapes in the confusion. You are left holding the paperwork.

choices.text: [Gauntling] Offer to pay for the arm.

outcomes.text: Your Gauntling pays the debt, in credits and in scrap, with a speech about the dignity of parts. Marrow tears up the warrant, and the Row cheers. Marrow, under her hard hat, is smiling. The Row repays you with the yard's best coil, and a pad.

Your Fenn finds the Gantry Clan's receipt for the arm: it was sold as scrap, three years ago, to the Gauntling. The sale was legal. The warrant is invalid. Marrow, who is not a fool, thanks your Fenn and leaves.

events.text: A half-built Gauntling, a torso and one arm on a hand-cart, is trying to push the cart up a ramp. A sign is taped to the cart: TAKE ME WITH YOU. A second sign: I AM NOT FINISHED. A third: THAT IS THE POINT. The Gauntling called Splice looks up at you with one lamp eye. 'I need a ship,' says the torso. 'I will build the rest on the way.'

outcomes.text: You lift the cart into the airlock. Splice is much lighter than they look, and enormously cheerful. By the end of the first week they have three legs, a toolbelt and an opinion about your wiring. Their first-day note stays pinned above the cart.

Your Gauntling unbolts a spare arm from the ship's locker and clamps it onto Splice, and Splice lifts it, turns it, flexes it. 'It is the best arm I ever had,' says Splice, with tears in the lamp. They climb aboard upside-down with joy.

choices.text: [Tinkerer] Help assemble the rest of them.

outcomes.text: Your tinkerer sets to work with a toolkit and a flask of tea. In three hours Splice has a full second arm, a left leg and a better attitude. Splice promptly hires them as a mentor. 'I will pay in parts,' says Splice.
'Thank you,' says the torso, and gets the cart halfway up the ramp. Behind you, a gasp, and the sound of someone helping.

events.text: Old Weld, who is more machine than anything else by now, keeps an Arc Core in a cage: a reactor that burns bright and mean and arcs a bolt through any soft thing in its room. 'Organic crew take two a second,' she says, cheerfully. 'Ion-hardened crew take nothing. It is a hell of a reactor.' She opens the cage. 'Run it for an hour in a closed room. Tell me how it feels.'

choices.text: Run it yourself. You are organic.

outcomes.text: You run it, wearing rubber gloves and a very large hat. You feel it in your fillings. At the hour mark Weld opens the door, looks at you, and nods. 'You are daft,' she says, with real warmth. She gives you the schematics.
You run it with the crew taking turns, ten minutes each. It is the funniest hour of the trip. Everyone has hair like a dandelion. Weld hands over the schematics.
A bolt finds the fillings of one of the crew. They will be fine in the morning. Weld, deeply impressed, signs.

Your Gauntling sits in the cage with the Arc Core for an hour, perfectly calm, lit up by bolts. 'Tickles,' they report. Old Weld whoops. She hands over the schematics, a coil of her best cable and a crate of washers.

choices.text: Line the room with 20 polymer first.

outcomes.text: You line the room with polymer. The bolts splash off, harmless. Weld says it is cheating, and also the first sensible thing anyone has done. She signs.
'Bring a hat,' says Weld. 'Hair will go.'

events.text: A Rustfang boat, the Lamp Post, is raiding the Row with what appear to be eight stolen work lamps for headlights. Her crew, in tarpaulins and welding masks, are shouting 'Hand over the parts!' It takes a moment to realise they are shouting at the Gauntlings, who regard them with deep, quiet interest, the way a butcher regards a pig.

outcomes.text: You open fire. The Row, delighted, pops up on every gantry to watch.

The Gauntlings stroll out in a line, unscrew their arms and hold them up like clubs. The Lamp Post's crew take one look and go. The Row cheers. A Gauntling shouts 'MORE!' and chases them for a kilometre.
The Lamp Post hits the Row. The Gauntlings dismantle the boat in six minutes flat, parts sorted by size. There are no survivors, only very upset pirates in their underwear.
Your Gauntling takes the lead of the charge, shouting 'FOR THE PARTS!' in a voice like an avalanche. The pirates fall back, and fall back again. The Row names a part after your Gauntling.
Your Kett skitter across the lane, eight arms swinging spanners in a perfect rhythm. The pirates look at them, say 'No', and retire.

after_win.text: The Lamp Post's hold is full of lamps, tarpaulins and a surprising amount of excellent spare parts. The Row helps you sort them, by size.

events.text: A rock the Row calls the Lodestone: iron-black, humming, and so magnetic that every loose tool within a kilometre has stuck to it. Spanners, pliers, hammers, a pair of false teeth, a ship's anchor. Gauntlings in rubber boots walk its surface picking tools off one by one. 'Mind your arm,' says one. 'It has opinions.'

outcomes.text: You wade through a rain of spanners, collecting the good ones and putting the bad ones back. The Lodestone keeps one of your own wrenches as payment.
Your belt buckle, your boots and your keys decide to fly off. You spend an hour chasing your own trousers.

choices.text: Cut a chunk of the Lodestone itself.

outcomes.text: You cut a chunk from the rock, and everything in the hold flies to it. Your own hull plates tug. You tow the chunk home on a long line, and sell it as the world's best fridge magnet.
The chunk takes off the moment it is cut and sticks to your bow. You are now a very fast, very magnetic ship. You cut it loose after two hours of grinding.

choices.text: [Gauntling] Walk it with your arm in a bag.

outcomes.text: Your Gauntling puts their arm in a rubber sack, grips a long pair of tongs, and walks the Lodestone like a lazy hiker. They come back with a sack of the finest tools in the Drift, including a perfect pair of false teeth.

choices.text: [Basalt] Hold the tools down with your own weight.

outcomes.text: Your Basalt stands on the Lodestone for an hour, letting the magnet pull the tools onto their back. They return covered in spanners, utterly calm. 'Pleasant,' they say.

events.text: A dead gunship, the Final Notice, drifts at the edge of the Row, and every plate on her hull crackles with blue-white light. Her reactor is still live, still arcing, still sending bolts through the walls. A scavenger who flew into her docking bay is frozen in a ball of static, waving politely. 'Do not touch the hull,' says the Row's warning buoy. 'Do not touch anything.'

outcomes.text: You edge through the arcing corridors with rubber gloves and a prayer. The reactor room is a cathedral of lightning. You pry loose a coil, a plate and a core, and walk out with your hair on end. The bank's last notice is pinned to the bridge door.
A bolt catches your shoulder. You drag yourself out, twitching. Everything you grabbed is still in your hand.
The reactor room surges while you are in it. Your gloves melt. You are lucky to be alive, and your hold is full.
A surge finds one of your crew in the corridor. They do not come out.

You edge through the arcing corridors with rubber gloves and a prayer. The reactor room is a cathedral of lightning. You pry loose a coil, a plate and a core, and walk out with your hair on end. The bank's last notice is pinned to the bridge door.
A bolt catches your shoulder. You drag yourself out, twitching. Everything you grabbed is still in your hand.
The reactor room surges while you are in it. Your gloves melt. You are lucky to be alive, and your hold is full.
A surge finds you in the corridor. You come out on your hands and knees, minus the gloves and most of the coil you went in for.

Your Gauntling walks into the arcing corridors, lit up like a Christmas tree, takes the whole reactor room apart in an hour and walks out whistling. 'Tickles,' they say. The haul is superb, with the bank's notice on top.
A surge stuns your Gauntling for three seconds in the middle of the room. They stand there, wired, until it passes. They are very calm about it.

choices.text: [Basalt] Walk the corridors. Rock does not conduct.

outcomes.text: Your Basalt walks the arcing corridors in no hurry, lightning crawling harmlessly down their back, and takes what they want. They return with a haul, a faint smell of ozone and a new haircut.
A bolt finds a seam in the rock, and your Basalt winces, politely. They carry on.

choices.text: Free the scavenger and leave the rest.

outcomes.text: You use a long pole to push the scavenger out of the static ball. He hangs in the lane, waving, then drifts off, grateful. His cargo drifts with him. He tosses you thirty credits from a very long way off.

events.text: A Gauntling on a repair skiff pulls alongside, politely, and looks at your ship with a hungry eye. 'That is a nice coil,' she says, pointing at your reactor housing. 'May I have it? I would like to be able to say I had one.' Her whole body is made of parts nobody wanted. Her lamp eye is tilted in hope.

outcomes.text: She cries real tears of oil. She takes the coil to her chest, installs it on the spot, and does a little lap of the ship. 'It is the best part I have,' she says. She gives you a box of her own spare parts.
She holds the little scrap in both hands like a jewel. 'It is a little thing,' she says, 'but it is mine.' She fits it into a space behind her ear and glows. She sends a gift back by comm.

choices.text: [Gauntling] Offer a part of your own.

outcomes.text: Your Gauntling unscrews their little finger and offers it. The other Gauntling is so moved she cannot speak. They trade fingers, and both go off with a spring in their step. The skiff's pilot leaves you a hold of cable as a thank-you.
She nods, tilts her lamp, and says, 'Thank you for hearing me.' She sets off, and the skiff's wake shines like a trail of stars.
